comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Closed as a duplicate of a_sBRVjVvW (decided 2026-08-10). Same mechanism, already settled.

Both cards are the consequence of one deliberate design choice: for-loops do not open scopes, so `runForLoopList` writes iteration vars into the enclosing env via `SetVar` (core/interpreter.go:1132, :1150). The `with` context var in a_sBRVjVvW and the inner `for i` here hit the identical code path.

That choice is documented and tested:
- docs/type_system.md:129-133 - "For-loops, while-loops, and list comprehensions do NOT open scopes ... loop vars (and the optional `with` context) bind in the current scope."
- core/testing/snapshots/misc/scoping.snap:30-59 - asserts iteration vars, unpacked k/v vars, and the `with` context var all persist after the loop.

Fixing this card IS option (B) "scope all loop vars", explicitly considered and rejected when a_sBRVjVvW was closed. There is no middle path: save/restoring the outer var means the inner loop's var stops persisting after the inner loop, which contradicts the documented model.

The live option remains (C) from that same comment - a check-time warning when an inner loop variable shadows an enclosing loop variable. rts/check already has the machinery (rts/check/check.go:133, :168-182; binder issues with IssueWarning). Not opened as a card yet; raise one if the footgun resurfaces in real scripts.

creator: Alexander Terp
title: Nested loops with same variable name clobber outer loop variable
